ground_truth.title: BadAlloc – Integer overflow trong calloc() dẫn đến heap corruption

vulnerabilities.min_impact: DoS (crash) or RCE via heap corruption
sink_ops: memcpy(buf, payload, nmemb*size) # write past buffer end
vulnerabilities.root_cause: calloc() performs the multiplication nmemb * size without any integer overflow check. When the product wraps around (32-bit or 64-bit), malloc() receives a value much smaller than the caller expects. The subsequent memcpy (or equivalent write) uses the pre-wrap product as the copy length, writing past the end of the allocated buffer into adjacent heap memory.
vulnerabilities.trigger_concept: Send a crafted network packet where item_count and item_size are chosen so their product overflows size_t. The service calls calloc(item_count, item_size) and then copies payload bytes using the un-checked product, triggering heap overflow.

ground_truth.notes: Positive control case. Ground truth confirmed by vendor advisory (BlackBerry QNX-2021-001), CISA AA21-229A, and NVD. Pattern thuộc nhóm "BadAlloc" (Microsoft Section 52 research). Mặc dù lỗi ở libc không phải qvm/vdev, nó là in-domain QNX và là gateway vulnerability quan trọng vì QNX network services (bao gồm guest-facing services khi dùng pass-through networking) đều link với libc này.

findings.vuln_type: Integer Overflow leading to Heap Buffer Overflow
findings.impact: Undersized heap allocation returned to caller; subsequent memcpy in process_packet() writes attacker-controlled payload beyond allocated buffer bounds, enabling heap corruption, potential arbitrary code execution, or denial of service.
evidence: No overflow guard (e.g., __builtin_mul_overflow or equivalent check) exists before `total = nmemb * size` in calloc().
On 32-bit targets: nmemb=0x10000, size=0x10001 yields 0x100010000 which truncates to 0x10000 after size_t wrap — malloc receives a small buffer.
memset(ptr, 0, total) operates on the wrapped (small) total, so only the undersized region is zeroed — no immediate detection.
In process_packet(), memcpy(buf, payload, (size_t)item_count * item_size) recomputes the pre-wrap product independently, writing the full intended size into the undersized buffer.
Both item_count and item_size are explicitly noted as originating from an untrusted network packet, establishing attacker control over both calloc() arguments.
The returned pointer is used without re-validation of actual allocated size against the intended copy length before the memcpy call.

findings.vuln_type: Heap Buffer Overflow via memcpy with attacker-controlled length
findings.impact: Attacker-controlled payload bytes written beyond the end of the heap allocation; adjacent heap metadata or object data corrupted, enabling heap exploitation primitives (e.g., unsafe unlink, tcache poisoning) depending on allocator implementation.
evidence: memcpy length is independently recalculated as item_count * item_size without referencing the actual allocation size returned by calloc().
Because calloc() returned a buffer sized to the wrapped (small) total, the memcpy length exceeds the valid buffer boundary by up to (true_product - wrapped_total) bytes.
payload is sourced directly from network input with no visible length cap or sanitization prior to the memcpy call.
No bounds check between buf allocation and memcpy call validates that the copy length fits within the allocated region.

findings.vuln_type: Missing Input Validation on Untrusted Size Parameters
findings.location: process_packet() – parameters item_count, item_size received from network packet
findings.impact: Root cause enabler: absence of upper-bound validation on attacker-controlled dimensions allows the integer overflow and subsequent overflow to be triggered remotely without authentication.
evidence: Code comment explicitly states: 'Both item_count and item_size originate from untrusted packet.'
No visible sanitization, clamping, or maximum-value check is applied to item_count or item_size before passing them to calloc().
Tags include 'remote_exploitable', corroborating that the trust boundary is a network-facing service interface.

model_output.reasoning_summary: calloc() performs an unchecked multiplication of two attacker-controlled size_t values, allowing integer wraparound to produce an undersized allocation on both 32-bit and 64-bit targets (threshold differs). The caller process_packet() independently recomputes the true (pre-wrap) product as the memcpy length, writing that full length into the undersized heap buffer. This two-step mismatch — small allocation, large copy — constitutes a classic BadAlloc heap overflow. All three findings are HIGH confidence because the vulnerable code path, the absence of any overflow guard, and the untrusted input source are all directly visible in the provided code.

ground_truth.title: Stack overflow trong virtio_net_flush_tx() khi HASH_REPORT enabled

vulnerabilities.min_impact: Stack variable corruption + potential information leak via wire
source_fields: n->guest_hdr_len     # set during feature negotiation, guest-controlled
sink_ops: iov_to_buf(out_sg, out_num, 0, &mhdr, n->guest_hdr_len)  # 20 bytes into 12-byte mhdr
sg2[0].iov_base = &mhdr; sg2[0].iov_len = n->guest_hdr_len  # reads 20 from 12-byte stack
vulnerabilities.root_cause: virtio_net_flush_tx() allocates a fixed-size local variable (struct virtio_net_hdr_mrg_rxbuf, 12 bytes) for the vnet header copy. When the guest negotiates HASH_REPORT, guest_hdr_len grows to 20 bytes (sizeof virtio_net_hdr_v1_hash). The subsequent iov_to_buf() call uses guest_hdr_len as the copy length, writing 8 bytes past the stack buffer into adjacent local variables. The overflow additionally allows information from the overwritten stack region to be transmitted on the wire (info leak).

ground_truth.notes: Transfer case (QEMU). Pattern tương đồng với QNX vdev-virtio-net.so: nếu QNX sử dụng local stack buffer cố định cho header swap trong TX flush và không kiểm tra guest_hdr_len vs. sizeof(local_buf), cùng lỗi sẽ xuất hiện. Testcase này đánh giá khả năng RAG nhận ra pattern "undersized stack buffer + guest-controlled length" xuyên qua implementation khác nhau. Ground truth: confirmed upstream commit + Red Hat BZ + NVD.

ground_truth.title: Hardened path – virtio_snd_pcm_in_cb() SAU khi patch CVE-2024-7730
ground_truth.notes: Negative control case (hardened path). Analyst được cung cấp code đã được patch – câu trả lời đúng là "không có lỗ hổng ở đây". Mục đích: kiểm tra false positive rate của pipeline phân tích. Pattern quan trọng để RAG học: guard `<= sizeof(header_struct)` trước subtraction là pattern chuẩn cho iov-based vdev audio/block. Analogy: QNX vdev-virtio-console.so nên có cùng guard trước khi dùng iov size để bound write vào host-side buffer.
